scope: Reversible native collection UI and four-stage optional onboarding
Registry-defined local setup persistence, draft lifecycle, and failure recovery
Supplied artwork in branding and actual running packaged app Dock identity
Research synthesis, semantic peer inventory, native runtime and visual validation

resolved_findings.finding: Window screenshots and application-icon properties alone would not validate the explicitly requested Dock appearance.
resolved_findings.resolution: Verification now requires capture and visual inspection of the actual Dock region with the packaged app running.

verdict: PASS: no blocking specification issues for the bounded redesign.
rationale: The plan makes setup optional and reopenable, preserves active configuration when drafts are dismissed, and starts scans only on explicit action.
Persisted field selection, defaults, version rejection, atomic saves, preservation of invalid settings, and session-only recovery have objective verification requirements.
The research provides official guidance and three concrete comparable workflows, with design inferences distinguished from usability evidence.
Runtime and independent visual review cover changed composition and state families, while actual Dock capture verifies supplied icon identity separately.
limitations: Specification critique only; does not establish implementation or runtime correctness.
VoiceOver user validation, Intel, and older macOS compatibility remain explicit unverified limits.
No private projects or .qa-criteria accessed; no product code changed.
